query: For a high-entropy alloy initially designed as a single-phase solid solution, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why it loses toughness or undergoes brittle fracture under mechanical loading in demanding engineering service? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, identify the applicable service and loading boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Thermal aging treatments applied at intermediate temperatures will promote enhanced L12 ordering in the FCC phase of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA (as-cast state with FCC + B2 phases). At around 600°C, this enhanced ordering combined with the formation of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries increases the apparent elastic modulus (APBE) and restricts dislocation cross-slip, resulting in planar slip and local stress concentrations that trigger plastic instability and brittle fracture. In contrast, aging at higher temperatures such as 750°C reduces L12 ordering and facilitates the formation of ductile transition zones along phase boundaries, thereby restoring toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in as-cast state (FCC + B2 phases)
generation.intervention: Thermal aging treatments applied at controlled temperatures, with a focus on an embrittlement condition at ~600°C and a recovery condition at ~750°C
generation.conditions: Aging regime within a specific temperature window (approximately 550–750°C) where chemical ordering kinetics and phase boundary evolution are significant; mechanical loading to evaluate fracture behavior under demanding engineering service conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced L12 ordering in the FCC domains (approaching Ni3Al stoichiometry) coupled with the formation of irregular, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries
generation.mechanism: Elevated APBE and elastic modulus in the ordered FCC domains restrict dislocation cross-slip, promoting planar slip. The combination of planar slip with stress concentrations at the jagged phase boundaries leads to local plastic instability and brittle fracture under mechanical loading. At temperatures near 750°C, reduced ordering and the emergence of ductile transition zones along phase boundaries mitigate these effects, restoring toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: A non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition where ductility is minimized at approximately 600°C (maximum ordering and jagged phase boundaries) relative to the as-cast baseline, with recovery of ductile behavior upon aging at around 750°C when ordering is suppressed.
generation.baseline: As-cast state of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA and conventional alloys exhibiting classical grain-boundary mediated embrittlement (e.g., temper embrittlement via impurity segregation)
generation.boundary: Service boundary defined by thermal exposure conditions: below ~550°C (no significant transition), in the 550–750°C range (brittle behavior due to ordering and phase boundary morphology), and above ~750°C (ductile recovery). Mechanical loading under conditions representative of demanding engineering service environments is required.
generation.uncertainty: The exact kinetic parameters of L12 ordering and the critical phase boundary morphology responsible for embrittlement are not fully quantified and may depend on alloy processing variations.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform systematic thermal aging experiments on AlCoCrFeNi2.1 HEA samples at temperatures below 550°C, around 600°C, and at 750°C. Use Transmission Kikuchi Diffraction (TKD) or TEM to examine the dislocation structures and crack initiation sites under controlled mechanical loading. Specifically, assess the presence of dislocation pile-ups and the degree of jaggedness at the B2/FCC phase boundaries, verifying that these features correlate with embrittlement only observed at ~600°C and not at 750°C.
measurements: Microstructural analysis (TKD/TEM) for identification of L12 ordering and phase boundary morphology
Mechanical testing for fracture toughness and ductility
Mapping of dislocation activity and crack initiation sites
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples aged at ~600°C do not exhibit enhanced L12 ordering, jagged phase boundaries, and localized dislocation pile-ups leading to brittle fracture under mechanical loading (or if similar features are observed in samples aged outside the predicted temperature window), then the hypothesis will be rejected.
